awd_titl_txt: Conference: Commutative Algebra in the South 2025
awd_abstract_narration:
This award supports participation in the conference “Commutative Algebra in the South 2025,” which will be held at Georgia State University on April 5 and 6, 2025.  The conference is focused on recent advances in commutative algebra.  The conference aims to foster new collaborations, including those among researchers from institutions located within the southern US.  The conference program will include short talks and a poster session that highlight results of early-career mathematicians, including those of graduate students.

Experts on a broad range of topics in commutative algebra and related areas will present recently obtained research results, and describe the techniques used to obtain them.  The conference will include invited lectures focusing on cohomology theory, homological algebra, prime characteristic methods, mixed characteristic commutative algebra, and combinatorial methods in algebra.  The website for the conference is https://cats-math.github.io

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
The goals of this project were to foster new connections among researchers at primarily southern institutions; to provide an opportunity for seven distinguished researchers, primarily located in the southern part of the United States, to present their findings to a broad audience during a 50-minute presentation; to provide a spotlight on research developed by individuals belonging to an underrepresented demographic; to provide a much needed opportunity for participants to interact and share ideas with one another, specifically those in the southern region of the United States; and to allow young researchers to summarize their research in a 10-minute “lighting-round”talk.
The conference organized provided the academic environment to discuss current directions of research and present new development in a major area of mathematics, commutative algebra. The conference hosted around 40 participants in a two day meeting in Atlanta, GA on the campus of Georgia State University. The participants were from major research centers in the south of United States, such as University of Alabama, University of Arkansas, Auburn University, Georgia Tech, Tulane, Georgia State University, among others. The category of researchers invited covered the entire academic spectrum, from graduate students to professors. An important percentage of speakers were assistant professors from schools in the region, in addition to a few distinguished experts. As proposed a lightning session followed by posters from graduate students and other young researchers has been organized and led to many fruitful conversations.
The conference itself is in part as a response to the rapid recent development of  the graduate programs in the mathematics departments in the south of United States, which have build active groups in commutative algebra leading to an increasing need to support these academic communities.
